sentences.text: The allegation against them is that they committed offence under Section 498-A of IPC.
The de facto complainant claims to be the wife of the 1 st petitioner/1st accused.
The 2nd petitioner is the mother and accused Nos.3 and 4 are the sisters of the 1st accused.

Accused No.5 is Jasir Ali.T.K.B vs Summayya on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14173905/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 6th accused is the brother of the 1st accused.
Accused No.7 is the wife of the 6th accused.
It is alleged that ever since the marriage of the de facto complainant with the 1 st accused on 28.04.2013, she was being subjected to mental cruelty demanding more gold and money by the accused.
2. The case was registered on the basis of Annexure-A1 complaint before the Station House Officer of Chandera Police Station, Kasargod.

After the completion of the investigation, the Sub Inspector of Police of Chandera Police Station has filed the Final Report alleging commission of the aforesaid offence by the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 7.
3.
In the present petition, the petitioners would contend that the offence alleged against them is not at all attracted in the facts and 2025:KER:39316 circumstances of the case.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. As already stated above, Annexure- A1 is the complaint preferred by the de facto complainant before the Station House Officer, of Chandera Police Station, on the basis of which the crime was registered against the petitioners.

On going through the aforesaid complaint, it is seen that there are only general, superficial and sweeping allegations against the petitioners that they have been mentally harassing the de facto complainant for not bringing more gold and money.

Apart from the perfunctory statement that the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 7 insulted the de facto complainant by innuendos, there are no substantial allegations about the physical or mental torture being inflicted upon the de facto complainant.
No specific dates are mentioned by the de facto complainant in her complaint about the alleged mental torture said to have been inflicted by the petitioners.

By adverting to Annexure-A2 FIR, the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the de facto complainant had married another person while her marital relationship with the 1st petitioner was subsisting.

Annexure-A2 FIR was registered at the Chandera Police Station in 2025:KER:39316 respect of the offence under Section 420 IPC against the de facto complainant on the basis of the complaint preferred by the 1 st petitioner about cheating him by marrying another person, and also expending his money making use of the ATM card supplied to her.

6. On a total analysis of the records, on which the prosecution is relying, in support of the allegations levelled against the petitioners, I find that apart from superficial and vague allegations, nothing could be brought out to show that the offence under Section 498-A is attracted.
In that view of the matter, it is highly necessary that the prosecution proceedings against the petitioners are to be terminated, to meet the ends of justice.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.
The proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 7 in C.C No.1062/2021 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Hosdurg, are hereby quashed.
